sentences.text: These appeals have been filed under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (the Act) by the third respondent/insurer and the claim petitioner respectively in O.P. (MV) No.761/2015 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Pala (the Tribunal), aggrieved by the Award dated 05/02/2019.
In these appeals, the parties and the documents will be referred to as described in the original petitions.

2. According to the claim petitioner, on 22/02/2015 at about 09:00 a.m., while he was pillion riding on motorcycle bearing no.KL-35 F-4156 through Erattupetta - Edamaruku road and when reached at Valiamangalam, car bearing registration no.TN-66/A-1536 driven by the second and 423 of 2020 2025:KER:60354 respondent in a rash and negligent manner knocked him down, as a result of which he sustained grievous injuries.
3. The first respondent-owner and the second respondent-driver filed written statement contending that the first and the second respondent are one and same person.
The vehicle was insured with the third respondent.
4. The third respondent-insurer filed written statement admitting the policy but denying negligence on the part of the second respondent.
The compensation claimed was contended to be exorbitant.
5. Before the Tribunal, no oral evidence was adduced by either side.
Exts.A1 to A8 were marked on the side of the claim petitioner.
Ext.B1 was marked on the side of the respondent.

6. The Tribunal on consideration of the documentary evidence and after hearing both sides, found negligence on the part of the second respondent-driver of the offending vehicle resulting in the incident and hence awarded an and 423 of 2020 2025:KER:60354 amount of 2,18,270/- together with interest @ 9% per annum from the date of the petition till the date of realisation along with proportionate costs.
Aggrieved by the Award, the third respondent/insurer and the claim petitioner have come up in appeal.
7. The only point that arises for consideration in these appeals is whether there is any infirmity in the findings of the Tribunal calling for an interference by this Court.

sentences.text: 8. Heard both sides.

9. It is submitted by the learned counsel for the third respondent/insurer that in the light of the dictum in Pournami v. Sandhya Sudheer, 2008 (4) KLT 817, it can be seen that there was negligence on the part of the claim petitioner as there were three persons on the motorcycle, which was involved in the accident.
It is submitted that the very fact that there were two pillion riders would show that the bike was carrying persons more than the permissible number.
This itself and 423 of 2020 2025:KER:60354 would show that the rider must have lost balance resulting in the accident.
Therefore, the argument advanced is that the second respondent/driver of the car alone cannot be held liable or held negligent in this case.

Per contra, it is submitted by the learned counsel for the claim petitioner that this aspect was considered by the Tribunal and for cogent reasons, had rejected the said contention of the third respondent and found that there was no negligence on the part of the rider or the pillion riders of the bike that was involved in the incident and hence there is no infirmity committed by the Tribunal calling for an interference by this Court.
10.
As per Ext.A6 final report, the second respondent herein, the accused, is alleged to have committed the offences punishable under Sections 279, 337, 338 and 304 (A) IPC.
As per the charge sheet, it is the second respondent- car driver, who was responsible for the accident.

In the light of the dictum in New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v. Pazhaniammal, 2011 (3) KHC 595, the charge sheet/final report is prima facie and 423 of 2020 2025:KER:60354 evidence of negligence and in case any person has got any objection to the findings or the opinion in the final report of the investigating officer, the burden is on him to disprove the same and to prove otherwise.

entities.text: New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v. Pazhaniammal, 2011 (3) KHC 595
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the case on hand, the final report is seen marked without any objection from the side of the third respondent/insurer.
No evidence has also been let in to show that the rider of the motorbike or the fact that there were more than one pillion rider had contributed to the accident.

That being the position, I do not find any infirmity in the finding of the Tribunal that it was the second respondent,
who was negligent resulting in the accident.
In the result, M.A.C.A.No.3056/2019 is dismissed.
11. The award of compensation by the Tribunal under the following head is challenged by the claim petitioner- Notional income
It is submitted by the learned counsel for the claim petitioner that the latter a tile worker was earning 18,000/- per and 423 of 2020 2025:KER:60354 month.

However,
the Tribunal fixed the notional income as 8,500/-, which is quite low going by dictum in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Company Ltd, (2011) 13 SCC 236, where the income of even a coolie is liable to be fixed at 10,000/-.

entities.text: Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Company Ltd, (2011) 13 SCC 236
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The claim petitioner is a skilled worker and therefore a higher notional income ought to have been fixed by the Tribunal.

Per contra, it is submitted by the learned counsel for the third respondent/insurer that the amount of 8,500/- fixed by the Tribunal in the absence of evidence is reasonable and that it does not call for any interference.
11.1. The fact that the claim petitioner was a tile worker is not seen disputed.
Going by the dictum in Ramachandrappa (Supra), the income of a coolie is liable to be fixed at 10,000/- in the year 2015.
Being a tile worker, I find that his notional income can be fixed as 13,000/-.

sentences.text: The materials on record show that the claim and 423 of 2020 2025:KER:60354 petitioner sustained the following injuries- " 1. Lacerated wound 3 x 2 cm on right knee.
2. Lacerated wound left side of scalp 5 x 2 cm.

3. Fracture 5th rib left.
4. Comminuted closed fracture shaft of right femur.
5.
Closed fracture left tibial condyle.
6. Fracture right illium."
He was hospitalised for a period of five days.
He also underwent two surgeries.
In all probability he might have been unable to work for a period of eight months.
Hence, he can be awarded an amount of 1,04,000/-, that is, 13,000/- x 8 months.
Pain and sufferings 13.
In the light of the injuries sustained, which include multiple fractures, I find that an amount of 80,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.
Compensation for loss of amenities 14.
An amount of 2,00,000/- was claimed.
The Tribunal granted an amount of 30,000/-.
In the facts and circumstances of the case, an amount of 50,000/- would be just and reasonable under this head.

The impugned Award is modified to the following extent:
